homepage.title: Only 8% Pass This Army Aptitude Test
homepage.summary: Work through 10 Army-style aptitude stages covering readiness, routes, signals, supplies, timing, observation, and calm reasoning.

footer.topicText: This test uses safe fictional Army-style aptitude scenarios about readiness checks, route sense, signals, supplies, timing, observation, order sequencing, stated safety rules, and calm logic under pressure.
footer.aboutText: This Army Aptitude Test is for entertainment and self-testing only. It is not an official army test, recruitment assessment, military training, tactical guidance, or qualification. Every question is designed to be solved from the information given in the prompt, without specialist military knowledge or country-specific terminology.

landing.quickStartText: The first checks are clean. Later stages combine routes, signals, supplies, timing, and stated priority rules.
landing.challengeText: There are 10 stages with 7 objective questions in each stage.

stageGroups.title: Readiness Checks
stageGroups.encouragement: Good start. Next, the test moves from kit checks into map and direction logic.

questions.prompt: A briefing says each team must carry a map, water, radio card, and first-aid kit before leaving. Team A has a map, water, and radio card. What is missing?
questions.explanation: The required list includes a first-aid kit, and that is the only required item not listed for Team A.

questions.prompt: A readiness board says green labels mean checked, yellow labels mean waiting, and red labels mean remove from use. A crate has a yellow label. What does the label mean?
questions.explanation: The prompt defines yellow labels as waiting, so the crate is not yet checked.

questions.prompt: A unit can move only when all three boxes are ticked: route confirmed, kit checked, radio tested. The route and radio boxes are ticked, but kit checked is blank. What is the correct status?
questions.explanation: All three boxes must be ticked. Since kit checked is blank, the unit is not ready yet.

questions.prompt: A vehicle check requires fuel above half, two spare water cans, and a working radio. Vehicle 4 has fuel above half, two spare water cans, and a radio marked faulty. Which check fails?
questions.explanation: The radio must be working, but Vehicle 4's radio is marked faulty.

questions.prompt: A packing rule says heavy items go at the bottom, fragile items go in the middle, and the route card stays on top. Which item should be placed on top?
questions.explanation: The rule explicitly says the route card stays on top.

questions.prompt: A team leader checks four names against four assigned radios. Noor has R1, Pavel has R2, Lina has R3, and Mateo has no radio. Who still needs a radio?
questions.explanation: Mateo is the only person listed without an assigned radio.

questions.prompt: A readiness rule says if the map is missing, stop the check and report it before counting supplies. The map folder is empty. What should happen next?
questions.explanation: The stated rule says a missing map must be reported before supplies are counted.

stageGroups.title: Map And Direction
stageGroups.encouragement: Route sense is warming up. Next, the signals and codes get tighter.

questions.prompt: On a grid, a marker starts at the center, moves one square north, then one square east. Where does it finish?
questions.explanation: One move north and one move east puts the marker north-east of the center.

questions.prompt: A route card says Point B is two kilometres after Point A, and Point C is one kilometre before Point B. Where is Point C compared with Point A?
questions.explanation: Point B is 2 km after A, and C is 1 km before B, so C is 1 km after A.

questions.prompt: A map key says a triangle marks a checkpoint, a square marks supplies, and a circle marks water. Which shape marks supplies?
questions.explanation: The map key defines the square as the supply marker.

questions.prompt: A team faces north. It turns right, moves forward, then turns right again. Which direction is it facing now?
questions.explanation: Facing north, the first right turn faces east. A second right turn faces south.

questions.prompt: A safe route must avoid blocked roads. The map shows Route 1 is open, Route 2 is blocked, and Route 3 is open. Which route must be avoided?
questions.explanation: The rule says blocked roads must be avoided, and Route 2 is the blocked route.

questions.prompt: A marker starts in the top-left cell of a 3 by 3 grid. It moves right, right, down. Where is it?
questions.explanation: Right, right moves to the top-right cell; down moves to the middle-right cell.

questions.prompt: A route note says the east track is shorter than the west track, but the west track is the only confirmed route. The instruction says use confirmed routes only. Which track should be used?
questions.explanation: The instruction prioritizes confirmed routes only, so the west track should be used even though it is longer.

stageGroups.title: Signals And Codes
stageGroups.encouragement: Signals decoded. Next, the test checks supply and load planning.

questions.prompt: A signal card says one short flash means stop, two short flashes mean move, and one long flash means return. The signal is two short flashes. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: The card states that two short flashes mean move.

questions.prompt: A radio code list says Alpha means check route, Bravo means check supplies, and Charlie means check radio. Which code means check supplies?
questions.explanation: The prompt defines Bravo as the code for checking supplies.

questions.prompt: A lamp pattern repeats red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue. What colour comes next?
questions.explanation: The repeating pattern is red, blue, blue, so the next colour is red.

questions.prompt: A code rule says the second letter gives the checkpoint number: A2 means checkpoint 2, B4 means checkpoint 4. What checkpoint does C3 mean?
questions.explanation: The rule says the number gives the checkpoint, so C3 means checkpoint 3.

questions.prompt: A message has three parts: route, time, load. The message reads Route 5, 14:00, 8 crates. Which part gives the load?
questions.explanation: The stated order is route, time, load, and 8 crates is the load.

questions.prompt: A flag rule says raised flag means ready, lowered flag means not ready, and crossed flags mean pause. The flags are crossed. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: The rule defines crossed flags as pause.

questions.prompt: A code sheet says odd numbers mean report to Point A and even numbers mean report to Point B. The message number is 16. Where should the report go?
questions.explanation: Sixteen is even, and the rule says even numbers report to Point B.

stageGroups.title: Supply And Load
stageGroups.encouragement: Supply planning is set. Next comes time and distance under clean constraints.

questions.prompt: A supply point needs 18 water cans. One vehicle carries 6 cans. How many full vehicle loads are needed?
questions.explanation: Eighteen cans divided by 6 cans per load equals 3 full loads.

questions.prompt: A crate limit is 20 kg. Three items weigh 7 kg, 6 kg, and 5 kg. What is their total weight?
questions.explanation: The total is 7 + 6 + 5 = 18 kg.

questions.prompt: A load rule says food crates go before tool crates, and tool crates go before spare parts. Which order follows the rule?
questions.explanation: The rule requires food before tools and tools before spare parts.

questions.prompt: A team has 24 ration packs. Each person needs 3 packs. How many people can be supplied?
questions.explanation: Twenty-four packs divided by 3 packs per person supplies 8 people.

questions.prompt: A supply rule says the heaviest crate must be loaded first. The crate weights are 12 kg, 15 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg. Which crate goes first?
questions.explanation: The heaviest listed crate is 15 kg.

questions.prompt: A vehicle can carry 10 boxes. It already has 4 boxes loaded. How many more boxes can it carry?
questions.explanation: The remaining capacity is 10 - 4 = 6 boxes.

questions.prompt: A kit list requires 5 torches and 5 batteries. The box has 5 torches and 4 batteries. What must be added to complete the kit list?
questions.explanation: The torch count is complete, but the battery count is short by 1.

stageGroups.title: Time And Distance
stageGroups.encouragement: Timing is under control. Next, observation and detail decide the score.

questions.prompt: A route takes 35 minutes. The team must arrive by 10:00. What is the latest start time?
questions.explanation: Starting at 09:25 and travelling for 35 minutes gives an arrival time of 10:00.

questions.prompt: A vehicle travels 12 km each hour. How far does it travel in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Twelve kilometres per hour for 3 hours equals 36 km.

questions.prompt: A checkpoint opens at 13:40 and closes 20 minutes later. What time does it close?
questions.explanation: Twenty minutes after 13:40 is 14:00.

questions.prompt: A march is split into three equal 4 km sections. What is the total distance?
questions.explanation: Three sections of 4 km make 12 km in total.

questions.prompt: A route is 18 km. The first vehicle has already covered 11 km. How many kilometres remain?
questions.explanation: The remaining distance is 18 - 11 = 7 km.

questions.prompt: A signal check takes 6 minutes, a route check takes 9 minutes, and both must be completed before departure. How long do the checks take in total?
questions.explanation: The total check time is 6 + 9 = 15 minutes.

questions.prompt: A team starts at 08:10, rests for 10 minutes at 08:40, then travels for 20 more minutes. What time does it finish?
questions.explanation: From 08:10 to 08:40 is 30 minutes, then a 10-minute rest ends at 08:50, and 20 more minutes ends at 09:10.

stageGroups.title: Observation And Detail
stageGroups.encouragement: Sharp detail work. Next, orders must be placed in the right sequence.

questions.prompt: A board lists Gate A open, Gate B closed, Gate C open, Gate D closed. Which gates are open?
questions.explanation: Only Gate A and Gate C are marked open.

questions.prompt: A label reads R-47B. Which option matches it exactly?
questions.explanation: R-47B exactly matches the label.

questions.prompt: A notice says use the blue folder, not the green folder. The table has blue, green, and white folders. Which folder should be used?
questions.explanation: The notice directly says to use the blue folder.

questions.prompt: A kit tag says expiry 06/28. Another says expiry 06/26. The rule says use the later expiry. Which tag should be chosen?
questions.explanation: 06/28 is later than 06/26.

questions.prompt: A checklist line says: compass - checked; radio - checked; lamp - unchecked; rope - checked. Which item is unchecked?
questions.explanation: The line marks only the lamp as unchecked.

questions.prompt: A route note says checkpoint marker is black with two white stripes. Which marker matches?
questions.explanation: The matching marker must be black and have two white stripes.

questions.prompt: A form says the correct box has code 8K2 and weight 14 kg. Which box matches both details?
questions.explanation: The box must match both the code 8K2 and the weight 14 kg.

stageGroups.title: Sequence And Orders
stageGroups.encouragement: The order checks are complete. Now the stated safety rules take priority.

questions.prompt: An order card says inspect, load, report, depart. What comes immediately after load?
questions.explanation: In the listed order, report comes immediately after load.

questions.prompt: A rule says confirm route before testing radio, and test radio before loading supplies. Which task comes first?
questions.explanation: The rule places route confirmation before radio testing and supply loading.

questions.prompt: A sequence repeats kit, map, radio, kit, map, radio. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The repeating sequence is kit, map, radio, so kit comes next.

questions.prompt: A four-step plan says Step 1: mark route. Step 2: check supplies. Step 3: send update. Step 4: move. Which step is send update?
questions.explanation: The plan explicitly lists send update as Step 3.

questions.prompt: A loading order says crates marked A go before B, and B goes before C. Which order follows the rule?
questions.explanation: The required order is A before B and B before C.

questions.prompt: A route sheet says first reach Point 1, then Point 3, then Point 2. Which point is reached last?
questions.explanation: The route sheet ends with Point 2.

questions.prompt: A check cycle is radio, fuel, tyres, radio, fuel, tyres. Which check comes after fuel?
questions.explanation: In the cycle, tyres comes after fuel.

stageGroups.title: Safety And Priority
stageGroups.encouragement: Safety priorities held. Next, pressure logic combines the constraints more tightly.

questions.prompt: The priority rule is safety first, then route speed, then comfort. Route A is slower but confirmed safe. Route B is faster but marked unsafe. Which route should be chosen?
questions.explanation: Safety is the first priority, so the slower safe route beats the faster unsafe route.

questions.prompt: The rule says if a hazard marker appears, stop and report before moving any supplies. A hazard marker appears near the supply point. What comes first?
questions.explanation: The stated rule says to stop and report before moving supplies.

questions.prompt: A priority card says protect people, then protect equipment, then save time. A leaking fuel can is beside a busy walkway. What should be addressed first?
questions.explanation: The highest priority is protecting people, and people are near the leak.

questions.prompt: A rule says no vehicle moves until the radio check and brake check both pass. The radio passes and the brake check fails. What is the status?
choices: Ready if the route is short
questions.explanation: Both checks must pass, and the brake check failed, so the vehicle is not cleared to move.

questions.prompt: The rule says unclear signals must be clarified before action. A signal is partly hidden by rain. What should the team do?
choices: Act on the visible part only
questions.explanation: The rule says unclear signals must be clarified before action.

questions.prompt: A priority rule says medical kit shortages are reported before food shortages. The team has one missing bandage and two missing meal packs. What should be reported first?
questions.explanation: The medical kit shortage is the missing bandage, and it has higher priority than food shortages.

questions.prompt: A safety board says enter only if the gate is open and the light is green. The gate is open, but the light is red. What is the correct decision?
choices: Enter because the gate is open
questions.explanation: Both conditions must be true. The red light means the entry condition is not met.

stageGroups.title: Logic Under Pressure
stageGroups.encouragement: You have reached the final test stage. Now each question combines multiple aptitude skills.

questions.prompt: A rule says only checked routes have a blue stamp. Route 4 has a blue stamp. What can be concluded?
questions.explanation: If only checked routes have a blue stamp, then a route with a blue stamp is checked.

questions.prompt: A supply point can accept either water or food first, but fuel must arrive after both. Water has arrived and fuel is waiting. What is still needed before fuel?
questions.explanation: Fuel must arrive after both water and food. Water has arrived, so food is still needed.

questions.prompt: If a route is unconfirmed, the rule says use it only if all confirmed routes are closed. Route A is confirmed and open. Route B is unconfirmed. Which route should be used?
questions.explanation: An unconfirmed route is used only if all confirmed routes are closed. Route A is confirmed and open.

questions.prompt: A code says M means move and H means hold. A second rule says if two codes conflict, follow hold. The board shows M and H together. What should the team do?
questions.explanation: The conflict rule says hold takes priority when M and H appear together.

questions.prompt: A planner says take the route with the lowest risk number. The options are Route A risk 4, Route B risk 2, Route C risk 5. Which route fits the rule?
questions.explanation: Route B has the lowest risk number, 2.

questions.prompt: A rule says a kit passes only if it has water, map, and radio. Kit X has water and radio. Kit Y has water, map, and radio. Which kit passes?
questions.explanation: Only Kit Y has all three required items.

questions.prompt: A checkpoint accepts teams before 16:00 only. Team A arrives at 15:50, Team B at 16:05, and Team C at 16:00. Which team clearly arrives before 16:00?
questions.explanation: Only 15:50 is before 16:00. Arriving at 16:00 is not before 16:00.

questions.prompt: A unit must use a confirmed route and arrive by 12:00. Route A is confirmed and takes 35 minutes. Route B is unconfirmed and takes 20 minutes. Starting at 11:20, which route meets both rules?
questions.explanation: Route A is confirmed and arrives at 11:55. Route B is faster but unconfirmed, so it fails the confirmed-route rule.

questions.prompt: A signal card says H means hold and M means move. The safety rule says a red marker overrides move signals. The board shows M and a red marker. What is the correct action?
choices: Hold because the red marker overrides M
questions.explanation: The red marker overrides move signals, so the team should hold despite the M signal.

questions.prompt: A load limit is 30 kg. A route requires water at 10 kg, radio kit at 4 kg, and two tool bags at 7 kg each. Does the load fit?
questions.explanation: The total is 10 + 4 + 7 + 7 = 28 kg, which is within the 30 kg limit.

questions.prompt: On a grid, the supply marker is one square east of center. A team starts at center, moves north, east, then south. It also must end on the supply marker. Does it meet the position rule?
choices: Yes, it ends one square east of center
No, it ends north-east of center
Yes, it ends one square south of center
questions.explanation: North, east, then south leaves the team one square east of center, which matches the supply marker.

questions.prompt: A sequence rule says inspect before load and load before depart. A timing rule says departure must be before 09:30. Inspect takes 10 minutes and load takes 15 minutes. What latest start time allows departure before 09:30?
questions.explanation: The two required steps take 25 minutes. Starting at 09:00 gives departure at 09:25, which is before 09:30.

questions.prompt: A form says choose the crate with code K7 and the later expiry. Two K7 crates expire in 06/27 and 06/29. A K8 crate expires in 07/29. Which crate should be chosen?
questions.explanation: The crate must have code K7, and among K7 crates, 06/29 is the later expiry.

questions.prompt: The priority rule is safety, then confirmed route, then speed. Route A is safe, confirmed, and takes 50 minutes. Route B is safe, unconfirmed, and takes 30 minutes. Route C is unsafe, confirmed, and takes 20 minutes. Which route wins?
questions.explanation: Safety comes first, so Route C loses. Confirmed route comes before speed, so Route A beats the faster but unconfirmed Route B.
